title: Both inclinations (Mishnah Berakhot 9:5)
hookLine: bless for the bad as for the good, and love God with both your inclinations
tomorrow: a dream you never think about again: is it a letter unopened?

lines: A WORD WITH AN EXTRA LETTER.
cards: Gratitude posts go up for the promotion and the acceptance letter. Nobody posts thankful for the layoff. The Mishnah does something stranger.
It says a person must bless for the bad just as for the good. And it proves it from a word that looks misspelled. So why would heart be spelled with an extra letter?

teach.b: The verse is the one recited in the Shema: "And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might." The ordinary Hebrew word for heart is lev.
But here the Torah writes levav, with the letter bet twice. One classic explanation: a doubled letter, a doubled heart.

So the Mishnah reads it: with all your heart means with both your inclinations, the good one and the bad one. The pull toward kindness, and the pull toward wanting, grabbing, sulking, all of it can love God.
Then it keeps going. With all your soul: even if your life is taken.
With all your might: and here it plays on the sound, for whatever measure is measured out to you, give thanks. That's the root of blessing the bad.
Elsewhere the same chapter gives the words for bad news: blessed is the true Judge. Here's what a skimmer would miss.
Blessing the bad isn't pretending it's good.

Bad news gets its own blessing, not the good-news one. The Mishnah doesn't ask anyone to fake a feeling. It asks for the whole heart, both halves, to stay turned toward God, even when the measure is hard.

how: Jews say a blessing on good news and a different one on bad news, 'blessed is the true Judge' (Baruch Dayan ha-Emet), which is also said on hearing of a death.

o: two hearts at war, until the good one finally wins
a choice between the good path and the bad one
the good pull and the bad pull, both able to love God

games.q: the verse, read closely — tap the pairs.
p: even if your life is taken

s: blessing for the bad means pretending it's actually good
bad news gets its own blessing, blessed is the true Judge, not the good-news one.
the Mishnah says even the bad inclination can love God
with all thy heart: with both your inclinations, the good and the bad.
levav is a copying mistake for lev
the Mishnah reads the doubled letter as a doubled heart: two inclinations.

games.q: your best friend didn't get into the program she wanted. she says, "everyone keeps saying everything happens for a reason. i just want to be sad." what does the Mishnah offer?
o: let it be bad: the Mishnah has a blessing for bad news that doesn't pretend.
help her find the reason fast, since she should be thankful for everything.
change the subject: blessings are for good news, so leave God out of it.
games.why: a person blesses for the bad as for the good, but with the bad news blessing: blessed is the true Judge. the whole heart, both halves, without faking a feeling.

practice: Name one hard thing out loud, plainly, without dressing it up. Then name one thing you still love with your whole heart. Let the two sit side by side for the rest of the time, neither one canceling the other.

wordCard.voice: Both inclinations: the Mishnah's reading of levav, the doubled heart, the good pull and the bad, both able to love God.

orig.note: Hebrew: your heart, in Deuteronomy 6:5, written with a doubled bet.

carryVoice: Keep it near: bless for the bad too, without pretending it's good. Thirty-four of fifty.
